From 57f3cb6c84159d12ba343574df2115fb18dd83ca Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Jason Gunthorpe <jgg@nvidia.com>
Date: Fri, 28 Nov 2025 20:53:21 -0400
Subject: [PATCH] RDMA/cm: Fix leaking the multicast GID table reference

If the CM ID is destroyed while the CM event for multicast creating is
still queued the cancel_work_sync() will prevent the work from running
which also prevents destroying the ah_attr. This leaks a refcount and
triggers a WARN:

   GID entry ref leak for dev syz1 index 2 ref=573
   WARNING: CPU: 1 PID: 655 at drivers/infiniband/core/cache.c:809 release_gid_table drivers/infiniband/core/cache.c:806 [inline]
   WARNING: CPU: 1 PID: 655 at drivers/infiniband/core/cache.c:809 gid_table_release_one+0x284/0x3cc drivers/infiniband/core/cache.c:886

Destroy the ah_attr after canceling the work, it is safe to call this
twice.

Link: https://patch.msgid.link/r/0-v1-4285d070a6b2+20a-rdma_mc_gid_leak_syz_jgg@nvidia.com
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Fixes: fe454dc31e84 ("RDMA/ucma: Fix use-after-free bug in ucma_create_uevent")
Reported-by: syzbot+b0da83a6c0e2e2bddbd4@syzkaller.appspotmail.com
Closes: https://lore.kernel.org/all/68232e7b.050a0220.f2294.09f6.GAE@google.com
Signed-off-by: Jason Gunthorpe <jgg@nvidia.com>

diff --git a/drivers/infiniband/core/cma.c b/drivers/infiniband/core/cma.c
index 95e89f5c147c..f00f1d3fbd9c 100644
--- a/drivers/infiniband/core/cma.c
+++ b/drivers/infiniband/core/cma.c
@@ -2009,6 +2009,7 @@ static void destroy_mc(struct rdma_id_private *id_priv,
 		ib_sa_free_multicast(mc->sa_mc);
 
 	if (rdma_protocol_roce(id_priv->id.device, id_priv->id.port_num)) {
+		struct rdma_cm_event *event = &mc->iboe_join.event;
 		struct rdma_dev_addr *dev_addr =
 			&id_priv->id.route.addr.dev_addr;
 		struct net_device *ndev = NULL;
@@ -2031,6 +2032,8 @@ static void destroy_mc(struct rdma_id_private *id_priv,
 		dev_put(ndev);
 
 		cancel_work_sync(&mc->iboe_join.work);
+		if (event->event == RDMA_CM_EVENT_MULTICAST_JOIN)
+			rdma_destroy_ah_attr(&event->param.ud.ah_attr);
 	}
 	kfree(mc);
 }
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of Modifications

### File: `drivers/infiniband/core/cma.c`

- **Added local variable**  
  Introduced a pointer `event` that points to `mc->iboe_join.event` to avoid repeated dereferencing.

- **Added cleanup for `ah_attr` after `cancel_work_sync`**  
  After calling `cancel_work_sync(&mc->iboe_join.work)`, a new conditional block checks whether the event type is `RDMA_CM_EVENT_MULTICAST_JOIN`. If so, it calls `rdma_destroy_ah_attr()` on `event->param.ud.ah_attr` to release the GID table reference held by this attribute.

### Relationship

The single change in `destroy_mc()` addresses a resource leak: when a CM ID is destroyed before the queued multicast join work executes, `cancel_work_sync()` prevents the work from running, but the `ah_attr` (which holds a reference to a GID entry) was not cleaned up. This caused a GID table reference leak and a kernel warning. The added code ensures that after cancelling the pending work, the `ah_attr` is properly destroyed (if the event was a join request) to release the reference. The cleanup is safe to call twice because `rdma_destroy_ah_attr()` already handles null and double-free scenarios (although the work is cancelled, so the event state remains).

You are a programming expert.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
cancel_work_sync(&mc->iboe_join.work);
```
Reason:  
When a CM ID is destroyed, `cancel_work_sync` prevents the multicast join event work from executing. The work handler would normally clean up the `ah_attr` (via `rdma_destroy_ah_attr`), but cancellation skips that step, causing a GID table reference leak and triggering a WARN. No subsequent cleanup of the already‑allocated `ah_attr` existed before the fix.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
cancel_work_sync(&mc->iboe_join.work);
if (event->event == RDMA_CM_EVENT_MULTICAST_JOIN)
	rdma_destroy_ah_attr(&event->param.ud.ah_attr);
```
Reason:  
After synchronously cancelling the work, the fix checks if the event stored in the multicast structure is a multicast join event (meaning the `ah_attr` was already allocated). If so, it explicitly destroys the `ah_attr` to release the GID reference. This is safe to call even if the work had already run and cleaned up, because the event type would then not match (e.g., it would be `RDMA_CM_EVENT_MULTICAST_JOIN` only if the work had not yet processed the event).
